newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-TAPIA DECISIONS ROMERO TO TAKE IBF JR BANTAMWEIGHT CROWN.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-TAPIA DECISIONS ROMERO TO TAKE IBF JR BANTAMWEIGHT CROWN.

text.p: The tumultous boxing career of Johnny Tapia reached a peak Friday when the showman claimed a 12-round unanimous decision over bitter rival Danny Romero to capture the International Boxing Federation junior bantamweight title.
Tapia used his superior boxing skills and was able to stay away from the power of Romero, his crosstown rival in Albuquerque, New Mexio.
"I refused to lose and refused to go down," added Tapia, who used to be trained by Romero's father. "Let bygones be bygones. I'll go on with my life and he can go on with his."
Judges Jerry Roth and Clark Sanmartino scored the bout 116-112, while Glen Hamada had it 115-113.

The 30-year-old Tapia, who overcame a three-year layoff as he battled against drug addiction, improved to 40-0-2, and remained unbeaten in 20 fights since returning to the ring in 1994 after kicking his habit.
Despite clowning around for much of the fight, the super-slick Tapia piled up points early and late, using a stinging left jab that bloodied the champion's nose.
Asked about the keys to victory, Tapia said: "My style and different movements. I had a good team on my side. I listened to the game plan and did it."
Romero disputed the decision, but gave Tapia credit.
"I thought I won," Romero said. "More power to him. He is the guy now. I had a game plan; it was nothing about power punching, it was more about boxing."
